\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جنازة} (janāza)}{جنازة (janāza)}]{\ar{جنازة} (janāza) — a funeral}

\label{lesson:AR-C314-janaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for anew, then the Arabic for to regain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جنازة}}
\textbf{\ar{جنازة}} — \emph{janāza} — \textquotedblleft{}a funeral\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حضر} \ar{الجيران} \ar{جنازة} \ar{الرجل} \ar{العجوز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaḍara al-jīrān janāzat ar-rajul al-ʿajūz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbours attended the old man’s funeral.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جنازة}} (\emph{janāza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-n-z} (Lane), where \emph{janāza} is the bier with the dead person upon it, and then the procession that carries it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janāza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janāza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaḍara al-jīrān janāzat ar-rajul al-ʿajūz.} — The neighbours attended the old man’s funeral.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for anew, then the Arabic for to regain, then say \emph{janāza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جنازة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A funeral\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{توفي} (tuwuffiya)}{توفي (tuwuffiya)}]{\ar{توفي} (tuwuffiya) — to pass away}

\label{lesson:AR-C314-tuwuffiya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to regain, then the Arabic for a funeral.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{توفي}}
\textbf{\ar{توفي}} — \emph{tuwuffiya} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{توفي} \ar{جدي} \ar{قبل} \ar{سنتين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tuwuffiya jaddī qabla sanatayn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather passed away two years ago.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتوفى}, \emph{yutawaffā}.

A polite word for to die, passive in form.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{توفي}} (\emph{tuwuffiya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-f-y} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to be complete, to fulfil\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Tawaffā} is \textquotedblleft{}to take a thing in full\textquotedblright{}; its passive, \emph{tuwuffiya}, is said of one whose life is complete.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuwuffiya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuwuffiya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuwuffiya jaddī qabla sanatayn.} — My grandfather passed away two years ago.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to regain, then the Arabic for a funeral, then say \emph{tuwuffiya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{توفي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pass away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دفن} (dafana)}{دفن (dafana)}]{\ar{دفن} (dafana) — to bury}

\label{lesson:AR-C314-dafana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a funeral, then the Arabic for to pass away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دفن}}
\textbf{\ar{دفن}} — \emph{dafana} — \textquotedblleft{}to bury\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دفن} \ar{الصياد} \ar{الكنز} \ar{تحت} \ar{شجرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dafana aṣ-ṣayyād al-kanz taḥta shajara.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fisherman buried the treasure under a tree.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يدفن}, \emph{yadfin}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دفن}} (\emph{dafana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-f-n} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to bury, to hide a thing in the ground\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شيع} (shayyaʿa)}{شيع (shayyaʿa)}]{\ar{شيع} (shayyaʿa) — to escort a coffin; to see off}

\label{lesson:AR-C314-shayyaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to pass away, then the Arabic for to bury.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شيع}}
\textbf{\ar{شيع}} — \emph{shayyaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to escort a coffin; to see off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شيع} \ar{أهل} \ar{القرية} \ar{الرجل} \ar{إلى} \ar{المقبرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shayyaʿa ahl al-qarya ar-rajul ilā al-maqbara.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The villagers walked with the man’s coffin to the cemetery.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشيع}, \emph{yushayyiʿ}.

The noun is \ar{تشييع}; \ar{شيع} \ar{ضيفه}: he saw his guest off.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شيع}} (\emph{shayyaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-y-ʿ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{}. It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to go along with one who is leaving\textquotedblright{}, and so with the dead.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shayyaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shayyaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shayyaʿa ahl al-qarya ar-rajul ilā al-maqbara.} — The villagers walked with the man’s coffin to the cemetery.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to pass away, then the Arabic for to bury, then say \emph{shayyaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شيع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To escort a coffin; to see off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قبر} (qabr)}{قبر (qabr)}]{\ar{قبر} (qabr) — a grave}

\label{lesson:AR-C314-qabr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to bury, then the Arabic for to escort a coffin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قبر}}
\textbf{\ar{قبر}} — \emph{qabr} — \textquotedblleft{}a grave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زارت} \ar{الأسرة} \ar{قبر} \ar{الجدة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zārat al-usra qabr al-jadda.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family visited the grandmother’s grave.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{قبور}, \emph{qubūr}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قبر}} (\emph{qabr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-b-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to bury\textquotedblright{}; \emph{qabr} is the place of burial.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zārat al-usra qabr al-jadda.} — The family visited the grandmother’s grave.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to bury, then the Arabic for to escort a coffin, then say \emph{qabr} again
